Basic Information

  • Host Institution: Heriot-Watt University & University of Edinburgh (Joint Programme)
  • Centre: Edinburgh Centre for Robotics (ECR)
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Duration: 4 years
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded (EPSRC CDT / UKRI AI Centre)
  • Location: Edinburgh
  • Official Website: https://www.edinburgh-robotics.org/

Project Overview & Significance

The Robotics and Autonomous Systems PhD programme is a , fully funded joint initiative between Heriot-Watt University and the University of Edinburgh, hosted by the Edinburgh Centre for Robotics (ECR). This 4-year programme is at the absolute forefront of global robotics research. It includes the CDT-D2AIR (UKRI AI Centre for Doctoral Training in Dependable and Deployable AI for Robotics) and the EPSRC CDT in Robotics and Autonomous Systems. The programme focuses on developing AI and robotic systems that are not only intelligent but also safe, reliable, and deployable in real-world environments. By bridging the gap between laboratory prototypes and robust, field-deployed robots, the research aims to revolutionise sectors such as healthcare, offshore energy, and manufacturing. Students get access to facilities, including the Robotarium, a state-of-the-art testing arena.

Research Themes & Objectives

The research covers a broad spectrum of robotics, including computer vision, machine learning, control systems, human-robot interaction, and autonomous navigation. The CDT-D2AIR programme specifically emphasises 'dependable' AI, ensuring that algorithms are transparent, fair, and robust. The objective is to train a new generation of roboticists who can design systems capable of operating safely and effectively in complex, dynamic environments. Projects often involve industrial partners, ensuring the research has a direct pathway to commercial and societal impact.

Training & Development

The 4-year programme includes a foundational first year of intensive training, covering both technical robotics skills and broader professional development. Students benefit from cohort-based learning, fostering collaboration across disciplines. The ECR provides access to hardware and software. Throughout the programme, students undertake placements with industry or international academic partners, ensuring they graduate with both a deep theoretical understanding and practical, deployment-focused experience. Graduates are highly sought after by leading tech companies, research institutes, and government agencies.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must hold a first-class or upper second-class honours degree in engineering, computer science, physics, or a related discipline. The programme is highly competitive. Funding is provided by EPSRC and UKRI, with specific eligibility rules regarding nationality and residency. Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in AI and physical robotics.

How to Apply & Official Contacts

Applications are open on a rolling basis. Prospective candidates should visit the official Edinburgh Centre for Robotics website to view specific project details and contact potential supervisors. General enquiries can be sent to the ECR administration team via their website.

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.
